claim: KTuner added a Quick Adjustment 'Boost Target Ramp Rate' for the Integra and all 11th gen Civics; it controls how aggressively boost ramps during high throttle so the turbo reaches target sooner.
quote: what this does is it controls how aggressive the Boost ramps up during High throttle situations
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Boost Target Ramp Rate is under Main Parameters > Quick Adjustments after loading the tune, with four options: improved ramp 1, improved ramp 2, aggressive ramp 1, aggressive disable ramp.
quote: go to main parameters after you load the tune go to Quick adjustments and right here you'll see boost Target ramp rate
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Test setup for the ramp-rate comparison: throttle responsiveness improved 3 with rev hang reduced, Advanced VSA factory, turbo responsiveness level 3, Normal 18 psi, Sport 21 psi, all runs in 21 psi second gear.
quote: normal was set to 18 support was set to 21 but I did all runs in 21 PSI
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: On the stock Integra/Civic 1.5T the boost curve stays nearly linear and peaks at about 14 psi even though the target was 16-18 psi in the stock run.
quote: we stay pretty linear hitting 14 at Max when the Boost Target should have been between 16 and 18
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: With factory boost levels plus KTuner's boost target ramp rate (improved 2), the boost curve and low-end power improve greatly versus stock ramp.
quote: with the factory boost levels and K tuners uh boost Target ramp rate it greatly helps the Boost curve
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: At 21 psi, improved ramp level 1 and 2 added power through to redline and evened out the boost curve around 4500 rpm versus factory ramp rate.
quote: here we see a significant difference in the way that turbo ramps up and sort of evens out at about 4 500
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Traction control/VSA must be fully disabled (pedal dance) for 0-60 and quarter-mile runs, otherwise a slip event pulls throttle back and power is lost; extra low-end boost from ramp rate triggers slip events on all-season tires.
quote: if you don't and the card detects the slip event it's going to pull back throttle
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: With the aggressive level 1 ramp at high boost the presenter felt clutch slip (car stuck at ~4000 rpm when flooring at 3000-3500 rpm), so he recommends 'improve level one' for anyone running high boost.
quote: if you're running high boost you should probably stick with improve level one
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: For the Civic Si/Integra, KTuner base maps are picked via New File and listing the car; a map with 18 psi Sport and 16.5 psi in the other target modes is recommended as the safe tune because the car runs hot with limited cooling.
quote: 18 PSI Sport and 16.5 in the other Target modes which is normal in Comfort
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Presenter says the car tends to run hot, and an aggressive driver on higher boost will see knock control rise and timing pull back, losing the power the tune was supposed to add.
quote: this car tends to run hot and it doesn't have proper cooling when you add more PSI
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: The presenter runs 21 psi Sport (18 psi other modes) on the Integra in cold New York weather; 22 psi felt fine with no clutch slip; he warns that higher psi needs caution.
quote: I use 21 PSI I'm not an aggressive driver I'm also a New York it's kind of cold out here
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Quick Adjustments include Throttle Responsiveness (Factory, Improved 1/2/3) where the differences between improved levels are subtle, plus a Rev Hang 'reduced' option.
quote: between one two and three the difference is very subtle it's up to you which one you want to use
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Turbo Responsiveness quick adjustment makes a clear difference in low/mid range, but it only works fully if 'Early Spool' is enabled under Quick Enables.
quote: you have to go to Quick enables and enable early spool this is very important
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: On the Si/Integra, when knock control correction reaches roughly 0.8 the driver can feel power being taken away; he suggests switching to a lower-psi target mode and driving to let knock control settle.
quote: once they're not controlled goals I would say like 0.8 you start feeling that difference in power
author: Another Rich Experience

claim: Dyno on 2023 Integra A-Spec 1.5T (PRL intake etc., PRL downpipe and front pipe): stock ECU 197 whp / 212 lb-ft; KTuner pre-loaded 23 psi base tune 222 whp / 249 lb-ft with the ECU actually reading about 22 psi.
quote: it's the 23 PSI tune. When I hooked up, the computer was still kind of really getting 22 PSI. So, at that, it made 222 horsepower
author: AHC Garage

claim: The KTuner high-end base tune warned that an upgraded clutch should be fitted first; this owner flashed it before the clutch and the clutch started to slip.
quote: this was the one at the the higher end of it uh that it they it said that you should probably have upgrade clutch before you do it
author: AHC Garage

claim: The dyno was done in very hot (about 98 F) and humid conditions, which the owner says hurts the numbers and heat-soaks the car even with cooling upgrades.
quote: super high heat in the shop. It's probably about 98° if not higher, super high humidity
author: AHC Garage

claim: On the same dyno, a Phearable Stage 1.5 race tune made more power than KTuner's base map (about 238-246 vs 222 whp-level numbers as noted) even though it is not tuned for the car's mods.
quote: it made more horsepower and more torque than the Ktuner base tune, but it's also not tuned custom for the car or the mods
author: AHC Garage

claim: After the Phearable tune, the owner saw a slightly rich AFR under full boost, which was acceptable for mountain driving.
quote: a little rich under full boost, but you know, we wanted it to be a little bit richer for the mountains
author: AHC Garage

claim: A 2023 Integra 1.5T with PRL intake, downpipe and intercooler baselined 200 whp; with a Hondata 91-octane tune plus ethanol mix it made 236 whp, then 241 whp / 231 lb-ft (tuner kept boost to a safe level).
quote: she baselined at 200 horsepower so right now I did the 91 tune and I played with it a little bit mixed some ethanol and so far she's making 236
author: Dardantuned

claim: Stock boost on a 2023 Integra baseline pull was about 14-15 psi; the tuner ramped to about 20 psi on the tune and notes that timing was kept low because there is no flex fuel sensor.
quote: it was about 14 15 psi from the factory
author: Dardantuned

claim: Two Step Performance baselined a stock 2025 Civic Si at 192 whp / 191 lb-ft on the dyno before flashing; the first KTuner tune used a 23 psi peak base map.
quote: right now we're at 192 to the wheel and 191 torque
author: Two Step Performance

claim: 2025 Civic Si needs the KTuner Connectivity Device (installed in place of the ECU connectors, powered from battery) because normal OBD flashing no longer works; sold via Two Step Performance.
quote: With Honda's 2025 updates, the usual tune reflash method needed another step
author: Two Step Performance

claim: Warm-up practice: with no oil temp gauge, wait until ECT is around 180 F before the first wide-open-throttle pull; run 91-93 octane for the 23 psi base map (87/85 won't work).
quote: I'd like to see it around the 180 Mark before we do but wide open throttle pull
author: Two Step Performance

claim: First-time KTuner V2 setup: a one-time lock process (agree compatibility, confirm V2); to get a vendor tune you send the vendor the serial number and software number from Tools > KTuner Information.
quote: you're going to go to tools up here. and find ktuner information and you'll have your serial number and your software number
author: Dale Does Stuff

claim: Flashing a vendor tune: File > Open Tune, then Tuning > Upload Tune, flash directly to the ECU; it erases the old tune first; after 'flash successful' turn the vehicle off and back on.
quote: you're going to go to tuning, upload tune
author: Dale Does Stuff

claim: A self-made tune on a 2025 Civic Si with only an intake was faster but made the clutch slip, so the owner reverted to the vendor tune.
quote: a tune that I created for my car that actually made my clutch slip. So, it was faster, but it's damaging the car
author: Dale Does Stuff

claim: Two Step's tune loads three in-car selectable maps: map 1 factory/valet, map 2 turbo response level 1 with 18 psi normal / 20 psi sport, map 3 turbo response level 3 with 18 psi normal / 24 psi sport.
quote: in map three here, we have our most responsive turbo response at level three
author: Dale Does Stuff

claim: Switching in-car maps: cruise control off, hold the Cancel button about 3 s until the map number shows (1-3); the car defaults to map 3 at startup when no OBD device is connected.
quote: make sure your cruise control is off. Then you're going to hold the cancel button for about 3 seconds
author: Dale Does Stuff

claim: Launch control RPM is adjusted in-car with clutch pressed and a short Cancel press, in the same cruise-button method; the owner left it at the vendor value.
quote: we're going to engage the clutch and then we're going to hit the cancel button very shortly
author: Dale Does Stuff

claim: For TunerView Bluetooth with a V1.2 the pairing PIN is the last five digits of the device serial number; V1.2 still needs unlocking with the laptop first, after which TunerView can flash, datalog and clear codes.
quote: you use the last five digits so the serial number here you'll use your last five digits it'll actually be the pin for your uh bluetooth
author: Mitch Mc

claim: TunerView app (Android) menu lets you flash maps (factory, 21 psi, vendor maps), start/stop datalogging, read and clear codes from the phone.
quote: you can flash any one of these right from here you can data log from here you can check check engine lights from here
author: Mitch Mc

claim: On the KTuner 21 psi starter map on a 2022 Civic Si, 91 pump gas in Canada, the maximum knock control seen was 0.52.
quote: most i've seen at a knock control is 0.52 on 91 pump gas in canada
author: Mitch Mc

claim: Owner reports severe clutch slip on the 23 psi KTuner map and says KTuner's notes recommend a clutch for the 22-23 psi maps; he suggests staying at 21 psi or lower on a stock clutch.
quote: i had severe slip on 23 and even in k tuners notes it it recommends a clutch for the 22 23 psi maps
author: Mitch Mc

claim: On a stock clutch with no bolt-ons, keep KTuner base maps under 22 psi because the clutch will slip; if running 22-23 psi, wait until about 3500 rpm before flooring it.
quote: if you are basically stock clutch and no bolt-ons anything like that i highly highly suggesting under 22 psi because the clutch will slip
author: Auto District

claim: The 'Starter 21 Dual Target 2' base map is recommended as the first map for 11th gen Civics and recommends 91+ octane.
quote: starter 21 dual target 2 which is kind of what i recommend a lot of you guys to start with
author: Auto District

claim: Quick Enables 'Early Spool' makes boost rise to roughly 20 psi within about a second on throttle (14-15 psi quickly in low gears) but the owner says it puts a lot of wear on the turbo.
quote: it puts a lot of wear on your turbo very quickly
author: Auto District

claim: Quick Enables also includes 'Advanced VSA' and an option to eliminate artificial knot control rise, useful if you monitor knock control.
quote: advanced vsa eliminate the artificial knot control rise that's the third option
author: Auto District
ktuner_table_or_setting: Quick Enables: eliminate artificial knock control rise

claim: Example Boost by Gear to reduce clutch wear: 12 psi in 1st, 14 in 2nd, 16 in 3rd, 20 in 4th, and up to ~21 in 5th/6th (target-limited by the tune).
quote: we're just going to go let's just say 12 second gear we'll go up to 14 third gear go to 16
author: Auto District

claim: Anti-lag and two-step are set under Main Parameters/Advanced Features: two-step rpm limit (example 2500) and anti-lag ignition target of -10 deg is what the presenter says many owners use.
quote: ignition target just gonna put that to uh negative 10 here because that's what a lot of guys online are doing
author: Auto District

claim: Flash dialog: 'Flash now' writes directly to the ECU (5-10 min); alternatively save to one of five tuning slots on the KTuner device, which TunerView (Android only) can switch via Bluetooth.
quote: you have five tuning slots so these slots here on the bottom one to five
author: Auto District

claim: During flashing the dash lights up with error codes; after 99-100% turn ignition off, wait at least 10 seconds, turn on and wait for the 'flash successful' prompt.
quote: i like to wait at least 10 seconds so kind of just do like the one mississippi
author: Auto District

claim: Phearable Stage 1.5 on an 11th gen Si (27WON downpipe, PRL front pipe, intercooler, intake): map 1 = 16 psi, map 2 = about 22-23 psi, map 3 = 25.5 psi; knock control read 0.49-0.52 on poor-quality fuel.
quote: First map is 16 PSI. Second map is 23 or 22, I believe. But third map is 25.5
author: SargentO_GiO 🟣

claim: The owner ran 14.6 s in the quarter-mile on the stock tune with only downpipe and front pipe, hoping for mid-14 low with more mods.
quote: I did I did 14.6 with a stock tune. Just with downpipe and frontpipe.
author: SargentO_GiO 🟣

claim: Owner's ranking of top 11th gen mods: KTuner first, then intercooler and downpipe; intercooler temps read 102 after several races while a stock car heat-soaked.
quote: First mod, KTuner. Second mod, intercooler and downpipe.
author: SargentO_GiO 🟣

claim: Phearable 1.5 map 2 on 91 octane with all bolt-ons and all-season tires on an 11th gen Si: knock control 0.64 in a Dragy run, traction-limited.
quote: let's see what the car can do ... Not control is 0.64 right now the car doesn't have any traction on the street
author: SargentO_GiO 🟣

claim: A 2022 Civic hatch 1.5T (stock turbo, PRL intake/intercooler/downpipe/front pipe, flex fuel, KTuner) remotely tuned by Derek Robertson (IMW) on E50 made 255 whp / 299 lb-ft.
quote: we ended up with 255 wheel and 299 torque I think that's pretty good
author: Axion Industries

claim: Owner says E30 is the 'ticket' on these 1.5T cars, E40 is stretching it, and E50 is roughly the maximum with the stock fuel system on pump.
quote: E30 is pretty much the ticket on these E40 stretching it
author: Axion Industries

claim: The hatch (non-Integra) 1.5T flowed less air than an Integra with similar mods, a gap the tuner and owner could not immediately explain even with an Si intake cam.
quote: somewhere where we're a little off on airflow so we're gonna have to kind of brainstorm
author: Axion Industries

claim: Installing KTuner on a catless-header 10th gen Civic RS 1.5T cleared the check-engine light caused by the O2 sensor and enabled the tune; Sport mode goes from 16 to 21 psi.
quote: as a new Boost from 16 PSI to 21 PSI
author: Leonardo Cruz

claim: Owner estimates the KTuner 21 psi map plus headers raises a 10th gen Civic RS from about 148-150 hp to roughly 200-215 hp (crank estimate, no dyno shown).
quote: then if it could go around 200 to 215 horsepower
author: Leonardo Cruz

claim: A near-stock 2023 Civic Si with PRL/Two Step bolt-ons and no tune made 218 whp / 210 lb-ft on a dyno on a hot day (car heat-soaked between pulls).
quote: the final result is 218 and 210 foot pound of Tor so uh well is a little off from my number
author: AHC Garage

claim: Owner of a 2025 Civic Si skipped the 27WON 271 downpipe because it requires a tune; bolt-ons that don't need a tune (front pipe, exhaust) were chosen to retain OEM reliability.
quote: I realized that I was like, "Oh, snap. You need to it it requires a tune."
author: Raul Rivera

claim: On a 2022 Civic Si with PRL intake, PLM downpipe/front pipe and other mods, flashing Phearable's tune set to 23 psi cleared the check engine light and brought back rev-matching.
quote: it did take off my check engine light. I did get my my rev match back
author: Wish

claim: KTuner setup flow: first connection prompts to lock the KTuner to the car/serial; then load the tune file onto the KTuner via USB at a computer, unplug and flash the car later from the KTuner screen (K menu > Flash) -- no computer needed in the car.
quote: you're gonna lock it to your car before you do anything once it's locked to your car then you can connect it to your computer
author: AudiuX

claim: TSP Stage 1 on a 10th gen Si: map 1 is factory boost (18 psi) with slightly improved throttle response, map 2 about 19-19.5 psi with level-2 throttle response, sport mode in maps 2/3 adds boost; rev hang electronic reduced to about half.
quote: in map one it's factory boost which is 18. in map 2 it's 19 i believe
author: AudiuX

claim: A third-party (MAP) intake whose tube diameter did not match the MAF housing gave bad airflow readings and cost about 7 mpg versus the PRL intake with correct MAF diameter; swapping fixed it.
quote: the airflow sensor diameter of the the tubing on that one is not is not right and so i was getting bad readings
author: AudiuX

claim: Logged IAT on the 10th gen Si: ~130-140 F at 70 F ambient with a centre-engine third-party intake, versus about 110 F at 100 F ambient with PRL intake and bigger intercooler.
quote: my intake temperature was getting up to 130 to 140 degrees fahrenheit and that was pretty surprising
author: AudiuX

claim: After KTuner + TSP Stage 1 + PRL intake + larger intercooler the owner's fuel economy rose from about 30 to about 37 mpg in map 1 normal driving, and falls back to ~30 in map 2 hard driving.
quote: i'm now back up to like 37 ish um if i'm just driving driving like normal in uh map one
author: AudiuX

claim: Intercooler hot-side tube popped off under boost after first install because of an under-tightened clamp; owner recommends re-checking clamps after the first drives.
quote: my turbo produced so much so much uh boost that it just popped this whole tube off
author: AudiuX

claim: After a flash the ECU starts with conservative timing and learns upward while there is no knock; the owner drives between flashes to let knock control learn down before comparing maps.
quote: when you first Flash and it learns itself higher and higher as you go based on uh if your car is not knocking
author: caraddict

claim: On a 2017 Civic Si/EX-T on Stage 1, knock control learned down to 0.56 then 0.49 (49%) after driving; the owner felt timing 'flat' at shifts (second to third) until learned.
quote: my knot control is uh learned itself down to 49% second gear 20 go God the timing feels flat when it shifts
author: caraddict

claim: Electronic rev hang remained with the KTuner stage 2 map but the owner found it minimized/gone with a custom tune on E21.
quote: I know with stage two it is definitely still there ... I have a strong suspicion that it is gone or close to it
author: caraddict

claim: Owner mixed ~E21 by adding about 2 gallons of E85 to a 12.6 gal tank of 91-92 pump for KTuner flex testing.
quote: let's go see what E21 does with stage two
author: caraddict

claim: 27WON turbo inlet pipe is a bolt-on that needs no tune and throws no CEL; it can give roughly +6 to +26 whp (and +4 to +15 lb-ft) if paired with an optimized tune, with better throttle response and less lag.
quote: you don't need a tune for this one, and you will not have a CEL as well
author: Justin V.

claim: If it is hot out or you run an aggressive map on 87 octane, knock control is unlikely to learn down much.
quote: if you run an aggressive map and you're on 87 octane or any kind of situation like that the knock control probably is not going to learn down
author: caraddict

claim: Owner has seen knock control values as low as 0.49 on the 10th gen 1.5T (spirited driving to speed learning); ordinary cruising does not make it learn down fast.
quote: I've seen 49 on their ones but anyway that's how you get it down quickly
author: caraddict

claim: MAF scale tuning method on KTuner (10th gen 1.5T manual): log with long-term fuel trim not learned, record while on throttle, stop logging before lifting off (coasting gives bogus zero trims), export log to CSV and average short-term trim per MAF-voltage row.
quote: you want to stop recording before you let off because the way I do it I look up the CSV
author: caraddict

claim: Owner hit short-term fuel trims over 40% after installing a larger-diameter intake MAF housing and corrected it by editing the MAF scale (per-voltage) values by the averaged trim, e.g. -8% at 0.98 V, -3.6% at 1.05 V, -5% at 1.29 V.
quote: it brought my trims from over 40's when I install this intake down to an acceptable level
author: caraddict

claim: A larger-diameter MAF housing (e.g. PRL race housing) reacts slower to airflow changes: the ECU applies a big trim (10-11%) on throttle changes and then settles to 1-2%.
quote: the ECU will apply a pretty big trim sometimes like 10 or 11 but then it quickly will stabilize down to one or two
author: caraddict

claim: To sweep the upper MAF scale, use a tall gear with slow roll-on from low rpm (not full throttle in a low gear) so airflow climbs smoothly through the voltage scale without jumping to the top.
quote: you got to be in a higher gear with more of a load that keeps the engine working at a lower rpm
author: caraddict

claim: CVT cars can use the same MAF-scale procedure but must watch voltage and sweep the curve because a fixed gear ratio cannot be selected (paddles can help).
quote: You can do the same thing you just have to watch the voltage and sweep through the curve
author: caraddict

claim: In KTuner LED setup, boost thresholds are entered in millibar absolute (not psi gauge): 12 psi boost at sea level needs 26.7 psi absolute converted to millibar, otherwise LEDs stay on.
quote: if I want 12 lbs of boost, I actually got to put 26.7 and then I got to convert it to millibar and then enter it
author: caraddict

claim: V2 menus: Flash lists Factory or up to five stored tunes; flashing shows the tune description, runs with ECU on, ends with 'cycle ECU power'; knock control now starts at 59 (0.59) after flash so you don't have to learn down from a high value.
quote: Cool thing now is they start knock control at 59. Uh so you don't have to learn down
author: caraddict

claim: Main Parameters includes MAF scale (needs changing for a different intake; PRL Cobra with street housing doesn't), rev limits, idle targets by coolant temp, closed-loop settings; catalyst efficiency codes from a downpipe can be disabled so burnouts don't cut power.
quote: if you get a code from the downpipe that is this code right here. Catalyst efficiency
author: caraddict

claim: Quick Adjustments include throttle responsiveness, eco-button behavior and 'throttle padding' (standard = harshest cut on lift; soft/medium nearest to stock rev hang); Quick Enables include 'disable rev hang'.
quote: standard throttle padding is the harshest cut when you let off the throttle
author: caraddict

claim: The 10th gen Starter map has two boost targets: Normal ~21 psi and Economy at factory boost, plus Final Boost Target and Boost by Gear tables (gear 1-6, 33 psi = not limiting).
quote: there's two boost targets. That one's for normal, so that's uh like 21 lb targeting
author: caraddict
ktuner_table_or_setting: Boost target tables / Boost by Gear

claim: Auto-logging settings (Settings) let you set rpm, throttle %, boost and speed thresholds for start/stop (e.g. log above 4000 rpm and >85% throttle); with defaults it starts at once and never stops.
quote: I always want it to log above 4 grand. But not unless I'm really on it
author: caraddict

claim: LED can be mapped to IAT: yellow at 120 F, orange at 135 F, red at 145 F, for monitoring heat on the 1.5T.
quote: at 120° it's 45% brightness and it's yellow. At 135° it gets brighter and it's orange
author: caraddict

claim: After enabling KTuner flex fuel on a car tuned on E10 pump gas (no other change), fuel trim immediately went to -7% because the flex tables assume zero ethanol at the base and add fuel for the extra 'ethanol' the sensor sees (pump gas measured ~11%).
quote: enabling flex filled and instantly like right away on a negative 7% field trip
author: caraddict

claim: Fix for the above: tune the base map for 11% ethanol as the zero point (set 0% flex corrections at E11) and step down about 5-6% each step, rather than retuning the MAF scale.
quote: make it at zero percent filled and 11 percent because that's what I was tutored by someone
author: caraddict
ktuner_table_or_setting: Flex fuel fuel correction vs ethanol %

claim: With flex fuel installed, the ethanol content reading takes a while to climb after adding E85 (tank must mix and sensor must see it): 11% showed first, then ~36% after 3 gal of E85 on a half tank.
quote: all right here we go it's finally climbing ... we're pretty steady at 36%
author: caraddict

claim: KTuner's wideband/AFR readout is lambda scaled to gasoline stoich 14.7, so on E85 the displayed AFR is still shown on the gasoline scale; target ~0.80 lambda equals ~11.8 on that scale (i.e. do not target gasoline numbers on E85).
quote: the sensor is giving a lambda value and the ECU applies the gasoline scale
author: caraddict

claim: Owner flex-fuel install notes: plastic-lined fuel line needed heat to fit barbed fittings; the ECT2 plug color differed on his 2017 manual car; total kit cost was about $200.
quote: I'll still be well under or maybe right around 200 bucks total for the whole thing
author: caraddict

claim: Tony Castillo (10th gen Si, Phearable 1.5 map 2 at ~19-21 psi, 225 whp / 260 lb-ft claimed) lost to a 10th gen Sport hatch running KTuner on ~E35-36 flex fuel in map 3, with the hatch on 107k miles and a stock clutch.
quote: i'm fluctuating between e35 and e36
author: Tony Castillo

claim: Owner says some E85 stage-2 cars on stock clutches do not slip while others do, e.g. a hatch on a KTuner base E85 map had a slipping clutch.
quote: his clutch slips
author: Tony Castillo

claim: Owner found it impossible to hold a steady load/rpm for MAF-scale logging on a modern car because the brake-plus-throttle trick is blocked by brake override, so MAF voltage cells can only be logged during sweeps.
quote: you're no longer able to hit the brake and give it gas and expect anything to happen
author: caraddict

claim: For 2020+ 10th gen Si (manual), KTuner added Quick Adjustment 'Throttle Padding' (standard/soft/medium) and an O2-sensor disable; setting soft/medium removed the harsh jerk on throttle lift-off that stock-based tunes had.
quote: right when you let off the throttle i mean it's it's nice fourth gear 20 300 rpm let off oh it's so smooth
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Throttle padding 'soft' made the car feel like rev hang was still on; 'medium' was a better compromise for this owner.
quote: with the throttle padding set to soft it almost felt like rev hang was on
author: Cameron Hill

claim: On the Phearable tune the same car showed ~21-22 psi in map 1 and 22-23 psi in map 2; the owner notes KTuner boost often reads different from the nominal map target and flashing can leave different results.
quote: map 2 i'll see 22 to 23 psi and then map one on this on the fearable tune i'll see like 2122
author: Cameron Hill

claim: After flashing, owner was told to drive ~15 minutes so the ECU goes to closed loop and warning lights clear.
quote: after you flash a tune i know that you're supposed to drive around for like 15 minutes about to put it into a closed loop
author: Cameron Hill

claim: After flashing a KTuner map on a 2021 10th gen Sport hatch, many dashboard warning lights stay on; they cleared after driving ~10 minutes on the highway.
quote: these lights are starting to go away so we're just gonna drive around uh for i would say about 10 minutes
author: Chris Time

claim: 0-60 on a 10th gen Civic Sport hatch with KTuner Stage 1 base tune: just under 6 s versus about 7 s stock (owner's stopwatch/app, not instrumented).
quote: 0 to 60 time with the k tuner is just about under six seconds so it's a huge improvement from the stock seven second
author: Chris Time

claim: The KTuner V2 screen can go to sleep and needs unplug/replug to wake; first connection prompts 'lock this ECU'.
quote: this screen automatically shuts off after a certain time so to get the screen to turn back on you simply just have to unplug and replug it
author: Chris Time

claim: TSP quotes Stage 1 (vendor claim) for 10th gen Si: 182 whp / 206 lb-ft stock to 237 whp / 281 lb-ft; tune made by Derek Robinson (IMW).
quote: stock with their tune it goes up to 237 wheel horsepower and 281 foot-pounds of torque
author: Cameron Hill

claim: TSP Stage 1 maps: map 1 = factory boost with improved turbo response and no rev hang; map 2 = 19 psi normal / 21 psi sport with improved turbo response; map 3 = 19 psi normal with a custom (undisclosed) sport boost. Switch via cruise Cancel hold, RES/SET to change.
quote: map to is 19 psi in normal mode 21 psi sport mode with improved turbocharger response
author: Cameron Hill

claim: To fully disable traction control for pulls: traction off/on with parking brake on, release brake, traction off/on again, then brake - VSA light blinks; otherwise ECU limits throttle.
quote: when traction control is on it doesn't completely allow the throttle body to open up
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Owner's TSP Stage 1 map 3 sport only showed ~20 psi (expected 24-25); TSP said it could be elevation or a bad upload. Re-flashing to stock and redoing the whole install from scratch fixed boost.
quote: flash your car back to stock and then pretend that you just got the key tuner in the mail and read you every single thing over again
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Maps: map 1 stock boost (~17 psi seen), map 2 = 19 psi normal / 21 psi sport, map 3 = 19 normal and sport ~23-25 psi depending on car/elevation.
quote: map 3 is 19 normal and a custom boost level which I see about 24 and some change
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Owner lost power on repeated runs due to heat soak on the stock intercooler and recommends an intercooler upgrade before other mods on the 10th gen Si.
quote: these cars are very susceptible to heat soak by an inner core upgrade first
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Owner says the 1.5T is good for roughly 350 hp on stock internals per forum consensus; a reported blown Si engine involved two-stepping on a cold engine on TSP Stage 1.
quote: he was two-stepping apparently on a cold engine obviously that's bad
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Disabling rev hang leaves the dual-mass-flywheel mechanical hang; cold-morning shifts can jerk if not shifted quickly, but shifting smoothly reduces the issue.
quote: you have to be very careful shifting this car because it will jerk on you
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Owner avoids flooring below ~3000-3500 rpm on the tune and rolls into throttle to protect the weak stock clutch (same clutch as the lower-power EX-T).
quote: I make sure that I'm at the very least 3000 rpm ... I try to be around 3500 before I even think about flooring it
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Stock tune loses power after about 5800 rpm while the TSP tune pulls strongly to 6200 rpm; owner shifts near 6200 rpm.
quote: on stuck tuned this car loses power it actually loses power after about 5,800 rpm
author: Cameron Hill

claim: On a CVT 2021 Civic Sport hatch, the KTuner Stage 1 base map allowed 87 octane but 91+ is recommended for best results; it advertises improved throttle response, reduced turbo lag and boost raised to 18 psi.
quote: for this tune you could still use 87 octane but to get the best results always go with 91 octane minimum
author: Chris Time

claim: Owner reports 0-60 of 5.8 s on a CVT 10th gen 1.5T hatch with KTuner Stage 1 base map and only a short ram intake (self-timed).
quote: i was surprisingly doing 0-60 in just 5.8 seconds and all i had was a short ramp intake
author: Chris Time

claim: Logged IAT on a CVT hatch reached 158 F while parked after a drive at 84 F ambient (heat soak); coolant was 170 F.
quote: this is 158 degrees fahrenheit uh it is currently 84 degrees out right now
author: Chris Time

claim: Intermittent KTuner V2 screen not turning on at ignition-on; owner was told a setting fixes it (see CAN Gateway).
quote: three tenths of the time i get in my car all i see is a non-functioning screen
author: Chris Time

claim: With a tune stored in the ECU the KTuner can be unplugged and the tune keeps running; the device only needs to be plugged in for live data.
quote: you do not have to keep this plugged in if you tuned your car because your tune is already saved on your ecu
author: Chris Time

claim: KTuner tunes are tied to ECU generation: 2017-18, 2019 and 2020 Civics have different ECUs, so a tune file for an earlier year will not work on a later one.
quote: 2017 and 18 have their own ECU. 2019 has its own and then 2020 has its own ECU
author: Cameron Hill

claim: V2 supports up to five tune slots, so tunes can be loaded and swapped on the car without a laptop; V1.2 needs the phone/TunerView app or head unit (Honda Hack) to switch.
quote: You have up to five slots
author: Cameron Hill

claim: V2 LEDs can be programmed to flash on thresholds such as coolant above 190 F or a knock count of 5.
quote: if my engine cooling gets over 190, it'll it'll flash at me or if my knot count hits five
author: Cameron Hill

claim: On 2019+ Civics (new CAN), the KTuner V2 does not wake with the car unless 'CAN Gateway' is set to Yes: put the car in accessory, tap the screen, open the menu and set CAN Gateway.
quote: all you have to do is put your car in at least accessory mode click anywhere on the screen to bring up this menu and then can Gateway
author: Cameron Hill

claim: TSP Stage 1 on 2020 Si: map 1 factory boost, map 2 factory normal / 21.5 psi sport, map 3 21.5 psi normal with custom sport boost; observed only ~20 psi in sport and ~18 psi in normal on the car, TSP advised logging and sending a datalog.
quote: map 2 is factory boost levels in normal mode and then in sport mode you get 21.5 psi
author: Cameron Hill

claim: Starting a TunerView/V2 datalog: tap the screen center and press Start Log; a blinking indicator top-right shows logging; log through all gears and full throttle to capture boost.
quote: in order to start a data log you just click in the middle and then start log
author: Cameron Hill
